Posted June 30, 2004
Analysis by Richard Cowan Sponsored by Advanced Nutrients.

The results of Canadian Parliamentary elections perfectly set the stage for a badly needed debate on cannabis prohibition.
See
We Live In Interesting Times: Chaos in Cannabis Prohibition Around the World. Does John Walters Really Want A National Debate on Marijuana Prohibition?
and links

Under a parliamentary system, when one party has a substantial majority, such as the Liberals had in the last Parliament, the Prime Minister is generally in a position to dictate legislation. Before the election, Prime Minister Paul Martin had indicated that he would just reintroduce the decrim bill that he had allowed to die in the last session. Now it won't be that simple.
See
UK Reefer Madness Spreads To Canada As Both Countries Move Toward Phoney Decrim Bills. One Cannabis User Dies of An Overdose, Another Commits Murder.
and
The Next Prime Minister of Canada Talks War On Us. Looming Prohibitionist Counterattack in Canada Proves Need for International Debate On Cannabis Prohibition.
and
The Prohibitionist Counterattack in Canada Escalates. Blatant Drive to Create DEAland Style Police State. Phony Decrim Bill Gets Even Worse.
and links

In the new parliament, the Liberals still have the largest position, but they no longer have a majority. Consequently, they will have to work with the leftish New Democrats, whose leader, Jack Layton, has called for legalization. Layton has also been very critical of DEAland interference in Canada's internal affairs, so he will not tolerate attempts by John Walters to intimidate Ottawa into following the prohibitionist party line.
See
John Walters Testimony To The Canadian Parliament. The Public Record Or What He Would Have Said, If He Was Not Afraid of Being Asked Embarrassing Questions. The Battle for Canada.

Also, the Bloc Quebecois, the Quebec sovereignty party, did very well in the election, and they recognize that there is a very strong anti-prohibitionist sentiment in La Belle Province.

My friend Marc-Boris St-Maurice, the Montreal based leader of the Bloc Pot and the Marijuana Party of Canada, tells me that Gilles Duceppe, the leader of the Bloc Quebecois represents the riding where the Montreal Compassion Society is located. He is friendly on the issue.

In any case, the new parliament will probably not convene until September, and cannabis reform is not going to be a priority issue for anyone. Consequently, the Canadian debate on the issue will not take place until well after the DEAland elections.

If Bush is re-defeated, and the various cannabis initiatives on the ballots in DEAland do well, this will make for a much better climate for a real debate in Canada.
See
Legalization Initiative To Be On November Ballot In Alaska. Good Prospects for Winning. It Should Influence Debate In Canada.
and
Richard Lee's Oakland Initiative To Be On November Ballot, But MPP's Nevada Initiative May Not Make It, And IT SHOULD NOT! Fiasco Embarrasses and Undermines Cannabis Movement With Mandatory Minimums!

In the meantime, two Canadian prohibitionists have had problems of their own.

Randy White, the prohibitionist Conservative member of Parliament from just south of Vancouver, was reelected, but he may have cost his party the election by suggesting that the Conservatives would use a loophole in the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedomsto void any Supreme Court decisions that they did not like. Consequently, White's influence in his party's councils has been greatly reduced. White is also in trouble for destroying the election signs of the Marijuana Party candidate in his riding.
See
As Kubby Refugee Hearings Resume. Government Makes Its Case Clear, If Not Well. And I Have Lunch With A Prohibitionist. Special Report to MarijuanaNews.com

And, Julian Fantino, the Police Chief of Toronto, was fired after one scandal too many.
See
Toronto Police Chief Supports Decrim -- At the Option of The Narks And " Education Or Treatment Programs " For Marijuana Users. The Therapeutic Police State. -- 2 Articles

Whom the gods would destroy, first they make prohibitionists.Now we just have to do our part.
See
It's The Stupidity, Stupid. How the Prohibitionist Ideology Has Wrecked The Republican Party and Undermined Democracy Everywhere. When Ideology Trumps Reality, The Result is Stupidity.
